EXTRACURRICULARS THAT ACTUALLY IMPRESS COLLEGES a guide for high school juniors by @fatimahs.guide 1. START A MICRO BUSINESS SOLVING A REAL PROBLEM Colleges love entrepreneurial initiative because it shows leadership, problem-solving, and real-world impact. Examples: ● Tutoring service: Teach middle schoolers coding, math, or SAT prep ● Social media management: Help local businesses with their Instagram or TikTok ● Lawn care or pet sitting: Classic neighborhood services with real income ● Reselling or Etsy shop: Thrift flipping, handmade jewelry, digital downloads ● Web design for small businesses: Build simple sites using free tools ● Event planning: Organize birthday parties or community events ● Content creation: Start a YouTube channel or blog teaching something you know 2. CREATE A COMMUNITY ADVOCACY PROJECT Find an issue in your local area and actually do something about it. Examples: ● Food insecurity campaign: Organize food drives or start a school pantry ● Environmental initiative: Beach cleanups, tree planting, petition for recycling programs ● Mental health awareness: Create a peer support group or organize wellness workshops ● Voter registration drives: Help eligible students register to vote ● STEM access for underrepresented students: Teach coding to younger kids ● Present to city council: Research a local issue and formally propose solutions ● Period poverty project: Collect and distribute menstrual products to schools or shelters ● Senior citizen tech help: Teach older adults how to use smartphones or video calls

3. BECOME A CERTIFIED EXPERT IN SOMETHING UNIQUE Certifications aren't just resume fillers—they're proof of real skills. Examples: ● CPR/First Aid certified Red Cross) ● Lifeguard certification ● Google certifications (data analytics, project management, digital marketing) ● Coding certifications (freeCodeCamp, Coursera, HarvardX CS50 ● Language proficiency DELE for Spanish, HSK for Chinese, JLPT for Japanese) ● Adobe Certified Professional Photoshop, Lightroom) ● EMT certification (check age requirements in your state) ● Referee or umpire certification for sports you play ● Food handler's permit REMEMBER Colleges value DEPTH over breadth. Pick a few of these and go all in rather than doing 10 things halfway. Show progression, leadership, and measurable impact.
